newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK post-budget poll sees rising rates.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK post-budget poll sees rising rates.

text.p: British interest rates are expected to rise in 1997 despite the cautious budget delivered by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, a Reuters survey of economists showed on Wednesday.
By the end of 1997, base rates will have risen to seven percent from six percent now, the median of 35 forecasts showed. Predictions ranged from six percent to 8.50 percent.

"I think the budget is going to prove a little more inflationary than expected. Combined with expectations of stronger growth next year, rates will have to be raised," said Sharda Persaud, European economist at San Paolo Bank.
For the middle of next year, the median of base rate forecasts was 6.5 percent and the range six to seven percent.
Contributors forecast the mean of 10-year gilt yields to be 7.90 percent at the middle of 1997, the predictions of the 30 contributors ranging from seven percent to 8.50 percent.
For end-1997, the mean of forecasts was slightly lower at 7.89 percent, from around 7.50 percent on Wednesday.

Most of those surveyed agreed that the budget delivered on Tuesday was cautious. Overall it was not expected to help the Conservative government's chances in the general election which has to be held by next May.
All but two of the 35 contributors are assuming a victory for the opposition Labour party, based on the latest public opinion polls, as the most likely scenario for their forecasts.
Richard Jeffrey, group economist at Charterhouse, assumes a Conservative victory and Sakura Finance is assuming the next government will be a Labour-controlled coalition.
